# @invisra/draft — LLM/agent reference

A dependency-free TypeScript library for generating engineering-style drafting
sheets: geometry primitives, a physical-unit SVG renderer, ANSI/ISO/architectural
paper sizes, title blocks, dimensioning, GD&T, hatching, and DXF/PDF export.
No 3D CAD kernel — everything is plain TS producing SVG (+ optional DXF/PDF).

This file is a dense API index for an agent writing code against this library.
For prose design rationale (why things work the way they do), see README.md.
For full per-symbol TSDoc, see dist/index.d.ts or the generated docs/ site.

```sh
npm install @invisra/draft
```

Mechanical-engineering elements — fasteners & threads, fits/limits & tolerance
standards (ISO 286 / ASME B4.1 / ISO 2768), surface-finish & weld symbols,
gears/springs/cams, hole & chamfer callouts, and tolerance stack-ups — now live
in the sibling package `@invisra/draft-mechanical`, which builds on this core
(`npm install @invisra/draft-mechanical`).

## Mental model (read this before writing code)

- **Units**: every number is millimeters, always. No unit suffixes on args.
  Convert only at boundaries with `toMM(value, "in")` / `fromMM(valueMM, "in")`.
- **Coordinates**: Y-up, origin bottom-left (+X right, +Y up) — standard
  drafting convention, not SVG's native Y-down. You never think in SVG space;
  `Sheet`/`renderSVGDocument` flip once at serialization.
- **`Renderable`**: anything with `toSVG(): string`. `Sheet.add()` accepts any
  `Renderable` — `DrawingElement`, `TextElement`, `Layer`, and every dimension/
  annotation/GD&T class satisfy it. New primitives don't need registration.
- **The core loop**: build `Path`s with geometry helpers or `Path` methods,
  wrap each in `new DrawingElement(path, opts)`, `sheet.add(...)` it, then
  `sheet.toSVG()`.
- **"Array, caller adds" pattern**: helpers that return multiple pieces
  (`centerMark`, `chainDimension`, `baselineDimension`, `hatch`,
  `hatchPattern`, `datumTargetPoint`, `axisCenterline`, `boltCircleCenterline`)
  return a plain array — loop and `.add()` each yourself; there's no wrapper
  class holding a group.
- **Classes vs functions**: most annotation/dimension/GD&T types are classes
  (`new LinearDimension(...)`, `new FeatureControlFrame(...)`) implementing
  `Renderable`. Pure geometry and formatting are plain functions.
- Most annotation classes are anchored at a point plus `angleDeg` (0 = +X
  axis, CCW positive) for their leader direction — `Callout`,
  `RadialDimension`/`DiameterDimension`, `ItemBalloon`,
  `DetailViewCallout`, `DatumFeatureSymbol`, `DatumTargetSymbol` all share
  this `(point, ..., { angleDeg, ... })` shape.

## Quick start

```ts
import { Sheet, TitleBlock, DrawingElement, roundedRectangle, circle, centerMark, LinearDimension, RadialDimension } from "@invisra/draft";

const sheet = new Sheet({ orientation: "landscape", borderStyle: "zoned" }); // defaults to ANSI A (Letter), "plain" border

sheet.setTitleBlock(new TitleBlock({
  title: "BRACKET, MOUNTING",
  drawingNumber: "DRW-1000",
  revision: "A",
  scale: "1:1",
  sheet: "1 OF 1",
  material: "AL 6061-T6",
  projection: "third-angle",
  drawnBy: "S. RICHS",
  drawnDate: "2026-07-08",
}));

const area = sheet.drawingArea; // usable region inside the border/title block
sheet.add(new DrawingElement(roundedRectangle(area.x + 20, area.y + 20, 80, 50, 6)));

const holeCenter = { x: area.x + 30, y: area.y + 30 };
sheet.add(new DrawingElement(circle(holeCenter.x, holeCenter.y, 4)));
for (const mark of centerMark(holeCenter, 4, 2.5)) {
  sheet.add(new DrawingElement(mark, { lineStyle: "centerline" }));
}

sheet.add(new LinearDimension({ x: area.x + 20, y: area.y + 20 }, { x: area.x + 100, y: area.y + 20 }, { offset: -12, orientation: "horizontal" }));
sheet.add(new RadialDimension(holeCenter, 4, { angleDeg: 45 }));

const svg: string = sheet.toSVG();
```

---

## Units

- `toMM(value, unit: "mm"|"in"): number`
- `fromMM(valueMM, unit): number`
- `MM_PER_INCH = 25.4`

## Geometry — points & vectors

`Point = { x, y }` (readonly, mm, Y-up).

- `point(x, y): Point`
- `addPoints(a, b)`, `subtractPoints(a, b)`, `scalePoint(p, factor)`
- `distance(a, b): number`, `midpoint(a, b): Point`
- `rotatePoint(p, angleRad, origin?): Point` — CCW positive
- `dot(a, b): number`, `magnitude(v): number`, `normalize(v): Point` (throws on zero vector)
- `perpendicular(v): Point` — rotates 90° CCW

## Geometry — bounding box

`BoundingBox = { minX, minY, maxX, maxY }`

- `bboxFromPoints(points): BoundingBox` (throws if empty)
- `unionBBox(a, b): BoundingBox`
- `bboxWidth(b)`, `bboxHeight(b): number`

## Geometry — segments

`LineSegment = { type: "line", start, end }`
`ArcSegment = { type: "arc", center, radius, startAngle, endAngle, counterclockwise }` — CAD-style (center/radius/angle), angles in radians from +X axis.
`EllipticalArcSegment = { type: "ellipticalArc", center, rx, ry, rotation, startAngle, endAngle, counterclockwise }` — rotation radians CCW; start/end are PARAMETRIC (eccentric) angles, radians. Reduces to a circular arc when rx===ry.
`CubicBezierSegment = { type: "bezier", start, control1, control2, end }` — cubic Bézier (two off-curve control points).
`Segment = LineSegment | ArcSegment | EllipticalArcSegment | CubicBezierSegment`

- `lineSegment(start, end): LineSegment`
- `arcSegment(center, radius, startAngle, endAngle, counterclockwise?): ArcSegment` (throws if radius <= 0)
- `ellipticalArcSegment(center, rx, ry, rotation, startAngle, endAngle, counterclockwise?): EllipticalArcSegment` (throws if rx/ry <= 0)
- `cubicBezierSegment(start, control1, control2, end): CubicBezierSegment`
- `arcPointAt(arc, angle): Point`; `ellipticalArcPointAt(arc, paramAngle): Point`; `bezierPointAt(seg, t): Point` (t in [0,1])
- `segmentStart(seg) / segmentEnd(seg): Point`
- `normalizeAngle(angle): number` — reduces to `[0, 2π)`
- `arcSpan(arc): number` / `ellipticalArcSpan(arc): number` — radians traversed in sweep direction, `(0, 2π]`
- `arcExtremaPoints(arc): Point[]` / `ellipticalArcExtremaPoints(arc): Point[]` — endpoints + extrema, for exact bbox
- `bezierExtremaPoints(seg): Point[]` — endpoints + axis-aligned extrema (derivative roots), for exact bbox

## Geometry — Path (Canvas2D-style builder)

```ts
class Path {
  moveTo(x, y): this;
  lineTo(x, y): this;
  arc(options: { center, radius, startAngle, endAngle, counterclockwise? }): this;
  ellipticalArc(options: { center, rx, ry, rotation?=0, startAngle, endAngle, counterclockwise? }): this; // angles parametric, radians
  bezierCurveTo(c1x, c1y, c2x, c2y, x, y): this; // cubic Bézier from current point; throws if no current point
  close(): this;
  isClosed(): boolean;
  getSegments(): readonly Segment[];
  boundingBox(): BoundingBox; // throws if empty
  flatten(angleStepDeg?): Point[]; // tessellate arcs to a straight-edge polygon
  toSVGPathData(precision?): string;
}
```
Single subpath only — no compound paths (that's why `centerMark`/`datumTargetPoint`/etc return arrays of 2 elements for X/cross shapes).

## Geometry — shape helpers (all return `Path`)

- `rectangle(x, y, width, height): Path` — CCW, `(x,y)` = bottom-left
- `roundedRectangle(x, y, width, height, radius): Path`
- `circle(cx, cy, radius): Path` — two semicircles (SVG can't do 360° in one arc)
- `ellipse(cx, cy, rx, ry, options?: { rotationDeg?=0, segments? }): Path` — two exact elliptical half-arcs by default; `segments` set → tessellated polyline instead
- `ellipticalArc(cx, cy, rx, ry, startAngleDeg, endAngleDeg, options?: { rotationDeg?=0, counterclockwise?=true }): Path` — open partial arc; angles PARAMETRIC (eccentric)
- `polyline(points, closed?): Path`
- `fitSpline(points, options?: { closed?=false, tension?=0 }): Path` — smooth Catmull-Rom spline that passes THROUGH every point, emitted as native cubic Béziers (n-1 spans open, n closed). `tension` 0=loose→1=straight chords. Needs ≥2 points.
- `centerMark(center, radius, overshoot?): [Path, Path]` — hole/round-feature center cross; use with `lineStyle: "centerline"`
- `axisCenterline(p1, p2, options?: { overshootMM?=3, symmetryTicks?=false, strokeWidthMM?, color? }): DrawingElement[]` — long-dash-short-dash axis/symmetry line, extended past both ends; `symmetryTicks` adds paired short solid ticks at each end (ASME symmetry-line). Elements already carry `lineStyle: "centerline"`. Throws if p1==p2.
- `boltCircleCenterline(center, radius, options?: { holeCenters?: Point[], overshootMM?=4, holeMarkRadiusMM?=2, strokeWidthMM?, color? }): DrawingElement[]` — companion to `boltCircle()`: dash-dot bolt circle + center cross through the pattern + a small centerline cross at each `holeCenters` entry. Throws on radius<=0.

## Geometry — construction (compute a layout instead of hand-placing points)

- `lineIntersection(a1, a2, b1, b2): Point | null` — infinite lines; null if parallel. `segmentIntersection(a1, a2, b1, b2): Point | null` — within both spans.
- `breakSegmentAtCrossings(a, b, obstacles: ({kind:"segment",p1,p2} | {kind:"circle",center,radius})[], gapMM): [Point,Point][]` — splits a→b into the pieces left after cutting a gapMM gap centered on each obstacle crossing (overlaps merge). `[[a,b]]` if nothing crosses, `[]` if fully covered or zero-length. AutoCAD DIMBREAK primitive; wired into `LinearDimension`'s `breakAt`.
- `lineCircleIntersection(p1, p2, center, radius): Point[]` (0/1/2, ordered along p1→p2). `segmentCircleIntersection(...)` — in-span only. `circleCircleIntersection(c1, r1, c2, r2): Point[]` (0/1/2, left-of-c1→c2-axis first; [] when separate/concentric/contained).
- Constructions (`geometry/construct.ts`): `circleThrough3Points(a, b, c): { center, radius } | null` (circumcircle; null if collinear). `tangentPointsFromPoint(center, radius, from): Point[]` (2 touch points, left-of-from→center-axis first; 1 if `from` on circle; [] if inside). `perpendicularBisector(a, b): [Point, Point] | null` (through the midpoint, ⟂, segment-length; null if coincident). `perpendicularFoot(p, a, b): Point` (orthogonal projection of p onto the infinite line ab).
- `filletCorner(p1, corner, p2, radius): { center, radius, tangentStart, tangentEnd, startAngle, endAngle, counterclockwise }` — tangent arc rounding a corner (p1/p2 give leg directions). Throws on collinear.
- `roundedPolyline(points, radius, closed?=false): Path` — rounds every interior corner (all if closed) into legs + tangent arcs; radius clamped per corner. Needs ≥3 points.
- `offsetPolyline(points, distance, closed?=false): Point[]` — signed miter offset (positive = left of travel); re-intersects adjacent edges. Straight miter (no self-intersection cleanup). Needs ≥2 points.
- `boltCircle(center, count, radius, options?: { startAngleDeg?=0, endAngleDeg?, clockwise?=false }): Point[]` — full circle, or an arc from start→end inclusive when `endAngleDeg` set.
- `linearPattern(start, step: Point, count): Point[]`; `rectangularPattern(origin, { columns, rows, dx, dy }): Point[]` (row-major).
- `polygonUnion(subject, clip): Point[][]` / `polygonIntersection(...)` / `polygonDifference(subject, clip): Point[][]` — Greiner–Hormann polygon clipping on rings of `Point`s (flatten a `Path` first); returns 0+ result rings. Difference with a contained clip returns outer + reversed hole ring (even-odd fill via `hatch()`). Simple polygons in general position; input winding doesn't matter.
- `polygonArea(points): number` — signed ring area (positive = CCW).
- `isometricProjection(p: {x,y,z}): Point` — standard 30° isometric (Y-up: +X right-down, +Y left-down, +Z up; unit axis → unit length). `projectIsoPlane("top"|"left"|"right", p: Point): Point` — lay a flat 2D point on a pictorial face (second coord runs up on left/right). `isoPolyline(points3d): Point[]` — project a polyline. `isometricAxisDirections(): { x, y, z: Point }` — the three axis unit vectors.
- `isometricEllipseAxes(plane, radius): { rx, ry, rotationDeg }` — the ellipse a circle projects to on a face (√3 major:minor; rot 0/top, -60/right, 60/left). `isometricCircle(plane, centerOnPlane: Point, radius, { segments? }): Path` — a hole/cylinder-end on a face as that ellipse (centerOnPlane is in-face 2D coords, projected internally). `isometricBox(size: {x,y,z}, { origin? }): Path[]` — visible edges of a prism (top loop + 2 front-face polylines).
- `class IsometricText implements Renderable { constructor(position: Point, content: string, options?: { plane?: "top"|"left"|"right", right?: Point, up?: Point, size?=3, anchor?, fontFamily?, color?, weight?, id? }) }` — text lettered onto an isometric face (glyphs sheared into the plane via an SVG matrix; not the upright TextElement). Per-plane default axes are non-mirrored; pass explicit unit `right`/`up` to override. Renders in PDF too (the PDF text pipeline now supports a full Tm; TextNode gained an optional `matrix`).
- `class IsometricLinearDimension implements Renderable { constructor(p1: Point, p2: Point, options: IsometricLinearDimensionOptions) }` — linear dimension on an isometric face. `IsometricLinearDimensionOptions extends DimensionStyle, ToleranceOptions: { plane: "top"|"left"|"right", offset /* signed, in-plane perpendicular */, text? }`. Endpoints are in face 2D coords; measures true in-plane distance (honors unit/zeroHandling/tolerance/count). Extension + dimension lines + flat arrowheads + value via IsometricText, all in the plane. SVG/PDF only (no native DXF).

## SVG core

- `Stroke = { color?, width?, dasharray?: number[], linecap?, linejoin? }`
- `LineStyleName = "visible" | "hidden" | "centerline" | "phantom" | "break" | "section" | "cutting"` — ASME Y14.2/ISO 128 line types; `LINE_STYLES: Record<LineStyleName, Stroke>` (`break`/`section` thin continuous; `cutting` = thick long-dash/short-dash cutting-plane line)
- `interface Renderable { toSVG(context?: RenderContext): string; bounds?(context?): BoundingBox | null }` — `RenderContext = { dimensionDefaults?: DimensionStyle, transform?: ViewTransform }`; zero-arg `toSVG()` implementations still satisfy it. `bounds()` is OPTIONAL (implemented by DrawingElement/TextElement/Layer/View/BlockInstance; dimensions/annotations omit it). `boundsOf(renderables, context?): BoundingBox | null` unions the measurable ones.
- Introspection & fit-to-view: `Sheet.contentBounds(): BoundingBox | null` (added content only), `View.contentBounds()` (children's true model extent) / `View.bounds()` (paper extent). `fitView(contentBoundsMM, area: { x, y, width, height }, options?: { marginMM?=0, maxScale?, name? }): View` — scales (aspect-preserved) + centers content into `area` (e.g. `sheet.drawingArea`); returns an empty View you `.add()` the content to.
- `class View implements Renderable { readonly scale; constructor(options: { scale, rotationDeg?=0, modelOrigin?={0,0}, paperOrigin?={0,0}, name? }); add(el): this; toPaper(modelPt): Point; toModel(paperPt): Point }` — scaled/rotated viewport: children authored in TRUE model coords, drawn at `scale` (2 = 2:1) and turned `rotationDeg` about modelOrigin (auxiliary/rotated views). Annotative: geometry scales+rotates but text/arrow/line-weight sizes stay paper-size, text stays upright (never turned), and dimensions read the true model value. Honored by DrawingElement/TextElement/dimensions/leader-callouts; position other annotations via `toPaper()`. Doesn't nest-compose. `ViewTransform = { scale, translate: Point, rotation?: number /* rad */ }`; `applyViewTransform(p, transform?)`, `Path.transformed(scale, translate, rotationRad?=0)`.
- `formatScaleRatio(scale): string` — `2`→`"2:1"`, `0.5`→`"1:2"`, `1`→`"1:1"`.
- `STANDARD_SCALES: readonly number[]` (ISO 5455 preferred, 50…1…1/10000), `nearestStandardScale(scale, scales?=STANDARD_SCALES): number` — snaps to the nearest preferred ratio in log space (3→2, 0.3→0.2); `isStandardScale(scale, scales?): boolean`. Pass a custom list for ASME (1/4, 1/8…). Throws on scale≤0.
- `class Block { constructor(name?); add(el): this; getElements(): Renderable[]; instance(options?: { position?={0,0}, scale?=1, rotationDeg?=0 }): BlockInstance }` — reusable symbol defined once in LOCAL coords. `class BlockInstance implements Renderable` — one placement; applies a view-style transform to the block's children (geometry scales/rotates, text upright) and COMPOSES with an enclosing View's transform (unlike View, which replaces). Emits no wrapper group (PDF-safe). `composeViewTransforms(outer?, inner): ViewTransform` composes two similarity transforms (`p → outer(inner(p))`).
- `class DrawingElement { constructor(path: Path, options?: { stroke?: Stroke | "none", lineStyle?: LineStyleName, fill?: string, id?: string }) }` — the basic stroked/filled `<path>` building block
- `class TextElement { constructor(position: Point, content: string, options?: { size?, anchor?: "start"|"middle"|"end", baseline?: "auto"|"middle"|"hanging", fontFamily?, color?, weight?: "normal"|"bold", id?, lineHeightMM?, maxWidthMM? }); lines(): string[] }` — carries its own Y-flip so Y-up positions render upright. Multi-line: `content` with hard `\n` breaks (and/or word-wrap to `maxWidthMM`, measured with AFM metrics) renders one `<text>` per line, stacked downward from `position` by `lineHeightMM` (default `size*1.2`) in paper units (line spacing, like text size, doesn't scale with a View). `lines()` returns the resolved display lines. `bounds()` boxes all lines (widest line × line count).
- `class Layer implements Renderable { constructor(options: { name, visible?: boolean }); add(element: Renderable): this }` — named `<g>`; nests (`layer.add(otherLayer)`); `visible: false` keeps content in output but `display:none`
- `renderSVGDocument({ widthMM, heightMM, body }): string` — wraps raw SVG body in a standalone physical-unit `<svg>`, applying the one Y-flip

## Paper sizes

`PaperSize = { name, widthMM, heightMM, sizeLabel }` (portrait/base orientation)

Constants: `ANSI_A..ANSI_E` (ANSI Y14.1), `A0..A5` (ISO 216, ≡ JIS A), `ARCH_A..ARCH_E1` (US architectural).
`PAPER_SIZES: Record<name, PaperSize>` (all of the above); `PaperSizeName = keyof typeof PAPER_SIZES`.
`customPaperSize(widthMM, heightMM, label?): PaperSize` — one-off size; any object shaped like `PaperSize` works anywhere one is accepted.

## Sheet & border

- `BorderStyle = "plain" | "zoned"` — zoned adds a numbered-column/lettered-row zone grid (e.g. "zone C3")
- `renderPlainBorder(widthMM, heightMM, marginMM, options?: { strokeWidthMM? }): string`
- `renderZonedBorder(widthMM, heightMM, marginMM, options?: { strokeWidthMM?, targetZoneSizeMM?, tickStrokeWidthMM?, labelSizeMM? }): string`
- `Orientation = "portrait" | "landscape"`
- `DrawingArea = { x, y, width, height }` — usable region inside border/title block

```ts
class Sheet {
  constructor(options?: {
    paperSize?: PaperSize;         // default ANSI_A
    orientation?: Orientation;     // default "landscape"
    marginMM?: number;
    borderStrokeWidthMM?: number;
    borderStyle?: BorderStyle;     // default "plain"
    zonedBorderOptions?: { targetZoneSizeMM?, tickStrokeWidthMM?, labelSizeMM? };
    dimensionDefaults?: DimensionStyle; // merged under every dimension/leader element (options win); e.g. ASME_INCH
  });
  readonly paperSize: PaperSize;
  readonly orientation: Orientation;
  readonly marginMM: number;
  readonly widthMM: number;
  readonly heightMM: number;
  get drawingArea(): DrawingArea;
  add(element: Renderable): this;
  setTitleBlock(titleBlock: TitleBlockLike): this;
  toSVG(): string;
}
```

## Multi-sheet sets

```ts
type SheetContext = { index: number; total: number; sheetLabel: string }; // "2 OF 5"
type SheetFactory = (ctx: SheetContext) => Sheet;

class DrawingSet {
  add(factory: SheetFactory): this;   // factory, not a ready Sheet — total isn't known until all are added
  build(): Sheet[];
  toSVGs(): string[];
}
```

## Title blocks

`TitleBlockLike = { heightMM: number; render(ctx: TitleBlockRenderContext): string }` — anything satisfying this works with `Sheet.setTitleBlock()`.

- `class TitleBlock implements TitleBlockLike` — classic ASME corner block (signoff grid + drawing ID). `constructor(fields: TitleBlockFields, options?: { widthMM?, labelSize?, valueSize?, strokeWidthMM? })`.
  `TitleBlockFields`: `title, drawingNumber` (required-ish); `revision?, size?, scale?, sheet?, material?, finish?, generalTolerance?: string[], projection?: ProjectionAngle, drawnBy?, drawnDate?, checkedBy?, checkedDate?, engApprovedBy?, engApprovedDate?, mfgApprovedBy?, mfgApprovedDate?`. `size` falls back to the Sheet's paper size label.
- `class ISO7200TitleBlock implements TitleBlockLike` — ISO 7200:2004 field set, single full-width column. `constructor(fields: ISO7200Fields, options?: GridTitleBlockOptions)`.
  `ISO7200Fields`: `title, legalOwner, identificationNumber, documentType, dateOfIssue, creator, approvalPerson` (mandatory) + `revisionIndex?, sheet?, size?`.
- `class GridTitleBlock implements TitleBlockLike` — fully custom title block from raw columns/rows/cells. `constructor(columns: GridColumn[], options?: { widthMM?, labelSize?, valueSize?, strokeWidthMM?, color? })`.
  `GridColumn = { widthFraction, rows: GridRow[] }`; `GridRow = { heightMM, cells: GridCell[] }`; `GridCell` = `LabeledCell { kind:"labeled", widthFraction, label, value?, lines?, valueSize?, align? }` | `CaptionCell { kind:"caption", widthFraction, text, size?, bold?, align? }`.
- `ProjectionAngle = "first-angle" | "third-angle"`; `projectionSymbol(center, angle, options?: { strokeWidthMM?, size? }): string` — real ISO 128/ASME Y14.3 cone+circles pictogram.
- Low-level: `gridHeight(rows): number`, `renderGridColumn(x0, y0, width, rows, style: GridStyle): string`.

## Tables

- `class RevisionTable implements Renderable { readonly heightMM: number; constructor(anchor: Point, entries: RevisionEntry[], options?: RevisionTableOptions) }` — `anchor` = top-left. `RevisionEntry = { rev, description, date, approved?, zone? }`. Pass entries **newest-first**. `RevisionTableOptions.columns?: ("zone"|"rev"|"description"|"date"|"approved")[]` (default omits zone).
- `class BOMTable implements Renderable { readonly heightMM: number; constructor(anchor: Point, entries: BOMEntry[], options?: BOMTableOptions) }` — `BOMEntry = { item, quantity, partNumber?, description, material? }`. Entries render top-to-bottom as given (reverse yourself for "item 1 at bottom"). `BOMTableOptions.columns?: ("item"|"quantity"|"partNumber"|"description"|"material")[]`.

## Hatching

- `hatch(boundary: Path | Path[], options?: HatchOptions): DrawingElement[]` — parallel section-lining, even-odd fill rule (pass `[outer, hole1, hole2, ...]` to leave holes unhatched automatically). `HatchOptions = { angleDeg?=45, spacingMM?=3, phaseMM?=0, strokeWidthMM?=0.18, color?="black", dasharray?, linecap? }`.
- `hatchPattern(boundary, pattern: HatchPattern, options?: { scale?=1, strokeWidthMM?, color? }): DrawingElement[]` — runs `hatch()` per line family in a named multi-family pattern.
- `HatchPattern = { name, description, families: HatchLineFamily[] }`; `HatchLineFamily = { angleDeg, spacingMM, phaseMM?, dasharray?, linecap? }`.
- Built-in material patterns (converted from AutoCAD `acad.pat`): `ANSI31` (iron/brick/stone), `ANSI32` (steel), `ANSI33` (bronze/brass/copper), `ANSI34` (plastic/rubber), `ANSI35` (fire brick), `ANSI36` (marble/slate/glass), `ANSI37` (lead/zinc/magnesium), `ANSI38` (aluminum). All in `ANSI_HATCH_PATTERNS: Record<name, HatchPattern>`.
- `knurl(boundary, options?: { pattern?: "diamond"|"straight", angleDeg?, spacingMM?=2, strokeWidthMM?=0.18, color? }): DrawingElement[]` — knurl-texture fill via `hatch()`; diamond = two families at ±angleDeg (default 45), straight = one (default 0). `knurlNote(pitch, pattern?="diamond"): string` → e.g. `"0.8 DIAMOND KNURL"` for a leader.

## Annotations

- `class CuttingPlaneLine implements Renderable { constructor(points: Point[], options: { viewDirectionDeg, label?, strokeWidthMM?=0.6, color?, legLengthMM?, arrowLengthMM?, arrowWidthMM?, labelSizeMM? }) }` — section marker; `points` (2+) for straight or offset/stepped sections; arrows point in `viewDirectionDeg` = direction of sight into the section (not toward the viewer).
- `sectionView(boundary: Path | Path[], options?: { cut?: { p1, p2, keep: "left"|"right" }, angleDeg?=45, spacingMM?=3, hatchStrokeWidthMM?=0.18, outline?=true, outlineStrokeWidthMM?=0.5, color? }): { region: Point[][], hatch: DrawingElement[], outline: DrawingElement[] }` — generates a section fill: section-lines the material region (holes open via even-odd), optionally clipping to one side of a `cut` plane first (each ring ∩ half-plane, Greiner–Hormann — keep the cut line off exact vertices). 2D fill generator over the outline you supply, not a 3D section.
- Named section helpers (`sectionHelpers.ts`, on `sectionView`): `halfSection(boundary, cut, options?): { region, hatch, outline, centerline }` (sections one half + returns the axis centerline along the cut plane); `revolvedSection(profile, options?): SectionViewResult` (thin 0.25mm outline default, in-situ); `removedSection(profile, { label?, labelSizeMM?, labelGapMM?, ...sectionViewOptions }): { region, hatch, outline, label? }` (`label` → a centered `ViewLabel` "SECTION A-A" below the profile).
- `class DetailViewCallout implements Renderable { constructor(center: Point, radius: number, options: { angleDeg, label, text?, strokeWidthMM?, color? }) }` — phantom-line circle + elbow leader to "DETAIL X".
- `class ViewLabel implements Renderable { constructor(position: Point, title: string, options?: { scale?, textSizeMM?=5, scaleSizeMM?, anchor?="middle", underline?=false, strokeWidthMM?=0.5, color? }) }` — bold view title ("SECTION A-A"/"VIEW A"/"DETAIL B" — caller owns the full string), optional smaller scale caption below + optional underline. The title the section/detail markers don't draw.
- `class ViewArrow implements Renderable { constructor(tail: Point, options: { angleDeg, label, lengthMM?=12, arrowLengthMM?=3.5, arrowWidthMM?=1.2, labelSizeMM?=5, strokeWidthMM?=0.6, color? }) }` — ISO 128-30 viewing-direction (arrow method) indicator: thick arrow in the sight direction + bold letter at the tail; the referenced view is titled with the same letter via ViewLabel. Both stay paper-size under a View transform.
- `class ExaminationSymbol implements Renderable, Explodable { constructor(jointPoint: Point, options: ExaminationSymbolOptions) }` — AWS A2.4:2020 clause 17 (nondestructive examination). `ExamSpec = { methods: string|string[] (RT/UT/MT/PT/VT/ET…, array joined with "+"), length? (extent or "25%"), count? }`. `ExaminationSymbolOptions = { angleDeg, arrowSide?: ExamSpec, otherSide?: ExamSpec, centered?: ExamSpec, allAround?, fieldExam?, tailNote?, radiationAngleDeg?, refLineLengthMM?, textSizeMM?, ...DimensionStyle-ish }`. Designation below line (arrowSide) / above (otherSide) / straddling (centered); length right of designation, count in parens away from line; `radiationAngleDeg` draws the radiation-direction arrow (§17.4). Not covered: sequenced reference lines.
- `class ItemBalloon implements Renderable { constructor(touchPoint: Point, itemNumber: string|number, options: { angleDeg, terminus?: "dot"|"arrow", radiusMM?, ... }) }` — BOM cross-reference balloon.
- `zigzagBreakLine(p1, p2, options?: { strokeWidthMM?, color?, amplitudeMM?=4, widthMM?=10 }): DrawingElement` — "long break" for a flat member; call once per edge.
- `cylindricalBreakLine(p1, p2, options?: { strokeWidthMM?, color? }): DrawingElement` — "S-break" for round shaft/tube; `p1`/`p2` span the diameter; call once (covers both edges).
- `freehandBreakLine(p1, p2, options?: { strokeWidthMM?=0.5, color?, amplitudeMM?=1.5, wavelengthMM?=6 }): DrawingElement` — ASME Y14.3 freehand "short break": thick wavy line; deterministic undulation (sine faired through fitSpline, ends on p1/p2), not randomized.
- `revisionCloud(boundary: Path | Point[], options?: { arcLengthMM?=8, bulgeRatio?=0.18, jitter?=0, seed?=1, strokeWidthMM?=0.35, color? }): DrawingElement` — scalloped-arc boundary around a changed area. `jitter` (0–1) varies bump size/bulge for a hand-drawn look; deterministic per `seed`.
- `class RevisionSymbol implements Renderable { constructor(center: Point, letter: string, options?: { shape?: "circle"|"triangle" /* default circle */, sizeMM?=6, strokeWidthMM?, textSizeMM?, color? }) }`.
- `class NotesBlock implements Renderable { readonly heightMM: number; constructor(anchor: Point, notes: string[], options?: { heading?="NOTES:", numbered?=true, startNumber?=1, textSizeMM?=2.5, lineSpacingMM?, indentMM?, maxWidthMM?, color? }) }` — numbered NOTES list, `anchor` = top-left, grows down; long notes wrap at `maxWidthMM` with hanging indent.
- `class FlagNote implements Renderable { constructor(center: Point, noteNumber: number|string, options?: { shape?: "triangle"|"pentagon"|"hexagon" /* default triangle */, sizeMM?=8, textSizeMM?, strokeWidthMM?, color? }) }` — numbered flag/delta note tying a feature to a NotesBlock entry.

## GD&T (ASME Y14.5)

- `GDTCharacteristic` (14 symbols): `"straightness"|"flatness"|"circularity"|"cylindricity"|"profile-line"|"profile-surface"|"angularity"|"perpendicularity"|"parallelism"|"position"|"concentricity"|"symmetry"|"circular-runout"|"total-runout"`.
- `renderCharacteristicSymbol(characteristic, c: Point, s: number, style?: { strokeWidthMM?, color? }): string`.
- `class FeatureControlFrame implements Renderable { constructor(anchor: Point, characteristic: GDTCharacteristic, toleranceValue: number, options?: FeatureControlFrameOptions) }` — `anchor` = bottom-left, grows rightward. `FeatureControlFrameOptions = { diameter?: boolean, modifier?: "MMC"|"LMC", projectedZone?: boolean, projectedHeight?: number, unequallyDisposed?: boolean, unequallyDisposedValue?: number, freeState?: boolean, tangentPlane?: boolean, statistical?: boolean, datums?: { letter, modifier? }[] /* 0-3 */, precision?=2, strokeWidthMM?, textSizeMM?, color? }`. Tolerance cell order (left→right): value, `Ⓤ`+amount (unequally-disposed profile), `Ⓜ`/`Ⓛ`, boxed `ST` (statistical), `Ⓟ`+height (projected zone), `Ⓕ` (free state), `Ⓣ` (tangent plane). `projectedHeight` implies `Ⓟ`; `unequallyDisposedValue` implies `Ⓤ`.
- `class CompositeFeatureControlFrame implements Renderable { constructor(anchor: Point, characteristic: GDTCharacteristic, segments: FrameSegment[] /* ≥2 */, options?: { precision?, strokeWidthMM?, textSizeMM?, color? }) }` — ASME Y14.5 composite frame: one shared characteristic symbol (tall cell) + stacked tolerance rows (upper PLTZF over lower FRTZF). `FrameSegment = { toleranceValue, diameter?, modifier?, projectedZone?, projectedHeight?, freeState?, tangentPlane?, unequallyDisposed?, unequallyDisposedValue?, statistical?, datums? }`. Columns align across rows; a row with fewer datums extends its last cell. Differs from stacking `FeatureControlFrame`s (which repeat the symbol).
- `class MultipleSingleSegmentFrame implements Renderable, Explodable { constructor(anchor: Point, rows: SingleSegmentRow[] /* ≥2 */, options?) }` — ASME Y14.5 multiple single-segment control: complete independent frames stacked, each row with its **own** characteristic symbol (full-width dividers), unlike the composite's shared symbol. `SingleSegmentRow = FrameSegment & { characteristic: GDTCharacteristic }` (rows may differ). Options same as composite.
- Datum-reference `▷` translation modifier: `DatumReferenceSpec.translation?: boolean` (rendered after the datum letter + material modifier) on any FCF/composite/multiple frame.
- GD&T application modifiers (`modifierSymbols.ts`, drawn on the leader/adjacent, not in cells): `allAroundSymbol(junction, opts?): DrawingElement[]` (circle at leader knee), `allOverSymbol(junction, opts?)` (double circle), `betweenSymbol(from, to, opts?: { fromLabel?, toLabel?, sizeMM?, ... }): DxfPrimitive[]` (`↔` double-arrow), `continuousFeatureNote(anchor, opts?)` (`CF`). Opts share `{ sizeMM?=3, strokeWidthMM?=0.25, color? }`.
- `class DatumFeatureSymbol implements Renderable { constructor(touchPoint: Point, letter: string, options: { angleDeg, leaderLengthMM?=8, boxSizeMM?=6, strokeWidthMM?, textSizeMM?, color?, filled?=true }) }` — tags a whole feature as a datum.
- `class DatumTargetSymbol implements Renderable { constructor(touchPoint: Point, letter: string, targetNumber: number, options: { angleDeg, areaSize?, areaText?, side?: "near"|"far", leaderLengthMM?=10, diameterMM?=8, strokeWidthMM?, textSizeMM?, color?, precision?=2 }) }` — split circle (letter+number / optional area size); tags a specific point/line/area. Upper half: `areaSize` → "⌀6.00" (circular), or `areaText` → free text e.g. "10X6" (non-circular; overrides areaSize).
- `datumTargetPoint(center, size?, options?): DrawingElement[]` — "X" marker (2 elements).
- `datumTargetLine(p1, p2, options?): DrawingElement[]` — phantom line + X at each end.
- `datumTargetArea(center, radius, options?): DrawingElement[]` — cross-hatched circular area marker. `datumTargetRectangle(center, width, height, options?)` — rectangular; `datumTargetAreaOutline(boundary: Path, options?)` — any closed Path (ellipse/polygon/…). All return `DrawingElement[]` (hatch + phantom outline).
- `inchToleranceBlock(options: { onePlace?, twoPlace?, threePlace?, fourPlace?: number, fractionalInch?: string, angularDeg?: number }): string[]` — US decimal-inch block tolerance, e.g. `[".X ±.03", ".XX ±.01", ".XXX ±.005", "ANGLES ±0.5°"]`; feed into `TitleBlockFields.generalTolerance`.
- `bonusTolerance(feature, actualSize): number` / `totalToleranceAt(feature, actualSize): number` / `virtualCondition(feature): { mmc, lmc, virtualCondition, resultantCondition }` — ASME Y14.5 material-condition calc. `FeatureToleranceInput = { featureType: "internal"|"external", minSize, maxSize, geometricTolerance, modifier: "MMC"|"LMC"|"RFS" }`. internal→MMC=minSize; external→MMC=maxSize. bonus = departure from MMC/LMC (0 for RFS); MMC modifier: external VC=MMC+t/RC=LMC−t, internal VC=MMC−t/RC=LMC+t (LMC reverses).

## Dimensioning

`DimensionStyle` (shared style, all optional, defaults via `DEFAULT_DIMENSION_STYLE`): `{ strokeWidthMM, arrowLengthMM, arrowWidthMM, extensionGapMM, extensionOvershootMM, textSizeMM, textGapMM, precision, unit?: "mm"|"in", zeroHandling?: "none"|"inch"|"metric", color, dualUnit?: "mm"|"in", dualPrecision?, dualZeroHandling? }`.
`resolveDimensionStyle(options): Required<DimensionStyle>`.
- `unit: "in"` displays the measured mm value as decimal inches (label only; geometry stays mm) and defaults `precision`→3, `zeroHandling`→`"inch"`. `zeroHandling`: `"inch"` drops the leading zero (`.250`, ASME Y14.5), `"metric"` drops trailing zeros (`0.5`/`24`), `"none"` (default for mm) keeps fixed decimals (`80.00`). A supplied `tolerance` is read in the display `unit`. AngularDimension ignores `unit` (degrees).
- Measurement format helpers: `formatMeasurement(valueMM, format): string` (converts mm→unit then formats), `formatValue(valueInUnit, format): string`, `applyZeroHandling(fixed, zeroHandling): string`, `resolveMeasurementFormat(fmt?): ResolvedMeasurementFormat`, where `format = number /* legacy precision, mm/none */ | ResolvedMeasurementFormat = { unit, precision, zeroHandling, inchDisplay?, fractionDenominator? }`.
- Inch display styles (`unit: "in"` only, via `DimensionStyle.inchDisplay` / `MeasurementFormat.inchDisplay`): `"decimal"` (default), `"fractional"` (`3/8`, `1 1/2`), `"architectural"` (`3'-6 1/2"`); `fractionDenominator` (power of two, default 16). Standalone: `formatFractionalInches(valueIn, denom?=16): string`, `formatArchitecturalInches(valueIn, denom?=16): string`.
- DMS angles: `AngularDimension` `angleFormat?: "decimal"|"dms"` → `30°30′`. Standalone: `formatAngleDMS(decimalDegrees, secondsPrecision?=0): string`.
- Dual dimensioning (ASME Y14.5 §2.4 bracket method): set `dualUnit` to append the value in a second unit — `50.00 [1.969]`; tolerance converted too (`50.00 ±0.50 [1.969 ±.020]`), prefixes repeat (`⌀25.40 [⌀1.000]`). Honored by LinearDimension (+chain/baseline) and Radial/DiameterDimension; text-override or AngularDimension → no bracket. Helpers: `resolveDualFormat(style): ResolvedMeasurementFormat|null`, `dualSecondary(valueMM, prefix, style, tolOptions): string|undefined` (inner secondary text, no brackets), `appendDual(primaryText, valueMM, prefix, style, tolOptions): string`.
- Document-wide defaults: `new Sheet({ dimensionDefaults: DimensionStyle })` merges that style UNDER every dimension/leader element's own options at render time (per-element wins), so a whole sheet is inches/one style in one place. Presets: `ASME_INCH` (`{unit:"in",zeroHandling:"inch"}`), `ASME_METRIC`, `ISO_METRIC` (`{unit:"mm",zeroHandling:"metric"}`). Flows through `Layer`s and into PDF export. Honored by dimensions + `Callout`; `AngularDimension` ignores an inherited `unit`. `mergeDimensionDefaults(options, defaults): options` exposes the merge; `Renderable.toSVG(context?: RenderContext)` and `RenderContext = { dimensionDefaults? }` carry it.

`ToleranceOptions` (shared by every dimension class): `{ tolerance?: number | { plus, minus }, toleranceDisplay?: "nominal"|"limits", basic?: boolean, reference?: boolean, count?: number, typical?: boolean, notToScale?: boolean }`.
- Plain number = symmetric `±X`; `{ plus, minus }` = asymmetric.
- `toleranceDisplay: "limits"` → stacked upper/lower limits instead of `±` (LinearDimension/AngularDimension only).
- `basic: true` → boxed ASME basic-dimension value. `reference: true` → parenthesized `"(40.00)"`.
- `notToScale: true` → underlines the value (ASME Y14.5 §2.2; SVG/PDF only, not DXF TEXT). `TextElement` gained an `underline?: boolean` option backing it.
- `LinearDimension` also takes `half?: boolean` (half/symmetry dimension: `p1` on the axis of symmetry, only the `p2` side drawn — one extension line + one arrowhead, line runs past the axis; displayed value is the **full** size = 2× the p1→p2 distance; native DXF gets the same full value).
- `count: 4` → `"4X …"` repetition prefix (ASME §1.9.5), outside any reference parens; `typical: true` → appends `" TYP"`. Applied in the shared `formatToleranceText`, so all dimension classes and native DXF DIMENSION text get them. A dual `[in]` bracket never repeats count/TYP/reference.
- Feature-shape prefixes: `RadialDimension`/`DiameterDimension` take `spherical?: boolean` → `SR`/`S⌀` (ASME §3.3.6); `LinearDimension` takes `square?: boolean` → `□` prefix (§3.3.7). In non-embedded PDF `□`→`SQ ` (like `⌀`→`Ø`).

```ts
class LinearDimension implements Renderable {
  constructor(p1: Point, p2: Point, options: LinearDimensionOptions);
}
// LinearDimensionOptions extends DimensionStyle, ToleranceOptions:
//   orientation?: "aligned"|"horizontal"|"vertical" (default "aligned")
//   offset: number   // signed, +90° CCW from measurement axis
//   text?: string    // override auto-formatted value
//   square?: boolean // □ prefix (ASME §3.3.7 square feature)
//   breakAt?: LineBreakObstacle[] // DIMBREAK: gap ext/dim lines at crossings (model coords); breakGapMM?=1.5. SVG only, not DXF.

class RadialDimension implements Renderable {   // "R 4.00" leader
  constructor(center: Point, radius: number, options: RadialDimensionOptions);
}
class DiameterDimension implements Renderable { // "⌀ 8.00" leader, same options shape
  constructor(center: Point, radius: number, options: RadialDimensionOptions);
}
// RadialDimensionOptions extends LeaderOptions, ToleranceOptions: { angleDeg, text?, spherical? (SR/S⌀, ASME §3.3.6) }

class AngularDimension implements Renderable {
  constructor(vertex: Point, p1: Point, p2: Point, options: AngularDimensionOptions);
}
// AngularDimensionOptions extends DimensionStyle, ToleranceOptions: { radius, text? }
// Measures CCW from ray-toward-p1 to ray-toward-p2 — order p1/p2 CCW or you get the reflex angle.

class ArcLengthDimension implements Renderable {  // ASME arc-length dim: radial ext lines to a concentric dim arc, tangent arrows, "⌒15.71"
  constructor(center: Point, radius: number, startAngleDeg: number, endAngleDeg: number, options: ArcLengthDimensionOptions);
}
// ArcLengthDimensionOptions extends DimensionStyle, ToleranceOptions: { offset /* radial paper mm to the dim arc */, counterclockwise?=true, symbol?=true /* ⌒ prefix */, text? }
// Value = radius × sweep (true arc length), honors unit/zeroHandling, scales in a View.

class JoggedRadiusDimension implements Renderable {  // ASME §5.9.4 foreshortened radius (true center off-sheet)
  constructor(arcPoint: Point, falseCenter: Point, radius: number, options: JoggedRadiusDimensionOptions);
}
// JoggedRadiusDimensionOptions extends DimensionStyle, ToleranceOptions: { jogSizeMM?=3, jogPosition?=0.5 /* fraction arc→falseCenter */, text? }
// Leader arc→(zigzag jog)→falseCenter, arrow at arcPoint; label reports the real R… (unforeshortened).

class MultiLeader implements Renderable {  // one note, several converging leaders — "3X ⌀5 THRU"
  constructor(targets: Point[], text: string | string[], options: MultiLeaderOptions);
}
// MultiLeaderOptions extends LeaderOptions: { landing: Point /* convergence point + shoulder start */, shoulderSign?: 1|-1 /* default: away from targets */ }
// A leader from each target to `landing`, then one horizontal shoulder into the note; arrowheads at targets unless arrow:false.

class Callout implements Renderable {  // generic elbow-leader note, e.g. "4X ⌀8.00 THRU"
  constructor(targetPoint: Point, text: string, options: CalloutOptions); // CalloutOptions extends LeaderOptions: { angleDeg }
}

class OrdinateDimension implements Renderable {  // ASME arrowless coordinate dim: extension line, no arrow, no dim line
  constructor(origin: Point, feature: Point, options: OrdinateDimensionOptions);
}
// OrdinateDimensionOptions extends DimensionStyle, ToleranceOptions: { axis: "x"|"y", offset /* signed extension length */, jog?=0 /* lateral dogleg */, text? }
// Value = |feature[axis] - origin[axis]|, from a common datum (origin reads 0). Honors unit/zeroHandling.
```

Stacking helpers (return arrays — loop and `.add()`):
- `chainDimension(points, options: LinearDimensionOptions): LinearDimension[]` — consecutive pairs, one shared offset.
- `baselineDimension(points, options: LinearDimensionOptions & { stackSpacing?=8 }): LinearDimension[]` — every point from `points[0]`, increasing offsets.
- `ordinateDimensions(origin, features, options: OrdinateDimensionOptions): OrdinateDimension[]` — one ordinate per feature from a common origin (include `origin` in `features` to show its `0`).
- `class OrdinateOrigin implements Renderable { constructor(origin: Point, options?: { diameterMM?=3, strokeWidthMM?=0.25, color?="black" }) }` — ASME §10.3 / ISO 129 origin indicator: a small open circle at the datum. Paper-size (position maps through a View transform, diameter doesn't scale); has `bounds()`. Pair with `ordinateDimensions`.
- `chainAngularDimension(vertex, rays, options: AngularDimensionOptions): AngularDimension[]`
- `baselineAngularDimension(vertex, rays, options: AngularDimensionOptions & { stackSpacing?=10 }): AngularDimension[]`
- (`rays`/`points` order matters: CCW, same reflex-angle caveat as `AngularDimension`.)

Leader internals (compose your own leader-based annotation):
- `LeaderOptions extends DimensionStyle = { leaderLengthMM?=8, elbowLengthMM?=4, arrow?=true }`
- `computeLeaderGeometry(start, angleDeg, options?): LeaderGeometry`
- `renderLeaderLine(start, angleDeg, geometry, options?): string`
- `renderElbowLeader(start, angleDeg, text: string | string[], options?): string` — text may be a stacked-line array
- `arrowhead(tip, direction, options?: { length?=3, width?=1, color? }): DrawingElement`

Tolerance/label formatting internals:
- `normalizeTolerance(input: number | { plus, minus }): { plus, minus }`
- `formatToleranceText(nominalText, options: ToleranceOptions, format: number | ResolvedMeasurementFormat): string`
- `formatLimits(measured, tolerance, format: number | ResolvedMeasurementFormat): { upper: string; lower: string }` — `measured`/tolerance already in the format's display unit.
- `estimateTextWidth(text, size, bold?=false): number` — real Adobe AFM per-glyph advance widths (Helvetica/-Bold, via `textWidth` in svg/fontMetrics), not a flat per-char factor. `textWidth(text, font: "Helvetica"|"Helvetica-Bold", sizeMM): number`.
- `renderDimensionLabel(center, measured, nominalText, textSizeMM, format: number | ResolvedMeasurementFormat, color, toleranceOpts, strokeWidthMM?, dual?): { svg, width, height }`
- `renderBasicBox(x, y, width, height, anchor, padding, color, strokeWidthMM): string`

## Export

### DXF (geometry + layers only — no text/dimensions/GD&T/title blocks)
- `pathToPolyline(path: Path): { vertices: { x, y, bulge }[], closed: boolean }` — exact arc-preserving conversion (bulge values), unlike `Path.flatten()`.
- `exportDXF(elements: (DrawingElement | { element: DrawingElement, layer?, linetype?: "CONTINUOUS"|"HIDDEN"|"CENTER"|"PHANTOM", colorIndex? } | TextElement | { text: TextElement, layer?, colorIndex? } | LinearDimension | RadialDimension | DiameterDimension | AngularDimension | OrdinateDimension | BlockInstance)[], options?: { precision?=6 }): string` — R12/AC1009 DXF. Geometry → POLYLINE (arcs as bulge; elliptical arcs tessellated); TextElement → one TEXT entity per line (height + anchor/baseline justification, default "TEXT" layer, STYLE/STANDARD table; multi-line text stacks downward — R12 TEXT is single-line, MTEXT is R13+). Layer/linetype auto-inferred from `lineStyle` unless overridden. Title blocks stay SVG-only.
- `importDXF(dxf: string): { elements: DrawingElement[], texts: TextElement[] }` — inverse of exportDXF. Reads ENTITIES: LINE/CIRCLE/ARC/LWPOLYLINE/POLYLINE (arcs recovered from bulges) + TEXT; recovers `lineStyle` from layer. Idempotent round-trip. Unsupported entity types (SPLINE/ELLIPSE/INSERT/HATCH/DIMENSION/MTEXT/3D) skipped; colors dropped.
- exportDXF also accepts `LinearDimension`/`RadialDimension`/`DiameterDimension`/`AngularDimension`/`OrdinateDimension` → native DXF DIMENSION entities (DIMSTYLE table + BLOCKS section with an anonymous picture block per dim + DIMENSION entity, on a "DIMENSIONS" layer). Dimtypes: linear 0/1, radius 4, diameter 3, angular 2, ordinate 6 (|64 for axis "x"). Angular pictures use ARC entities. MTEXT unused (R13+; writer is R12). `LinearDimension.dimensionData()` and the others' `dimensionDXF(): DimensionDXFData` expose the definition/picture the exporter reads.
- exportDXF also accepts GD&T annotations — `FeatureControlFrame`, `CompositeFeatureControlFrame`, `MultipleSingleSegmentFrame`, `DatumFeatureSymbol`, `DatumTargetSymbol` (bare, or wrapped as `{ gdt, layer?, colorIndex? }`) — exploded into POLYLINE/TEXT on a "GDT" layer (R12 has no native feature-control-frame entity). Each implements `Explodable` (`toElements(): (DrawingElement|TextElement)[]`), and its `toSVG()` derives from the same list so SVG/DXF can't drift.
- exportDXF also accepts title blocks/tables, exploded onto a "TITLEBLOCK" layer: `{ titleBlock, context: { sheetWidthMM, marginMM, paperSizeLabel? }, layer?, colorIndex? }` for a `TitleBlock`/`GridTitleBlock`/`ISO7200TitleBlock` (context positions it bottom-right, same as a Sheet), or a bare anchored `BOMTable`/`RevisionTable`. Title blocks expose `renderElements(ctx)`, tables `toElements()`. For a whole sheet at once use `sheet.toDXF()` (below).
- exportDXF accepts any `Explodable` annotation (bare) onto an "ANNOTATIONS" layer — the callout/leader family (`Callout`, `MultiLeader`, `DetailViewCallout`), the symbol/tag family (`ExaminationSymbol`, `ItemBalloon`, `RevisionSymbol`, `OrdinateOrigin`), the notes/data-table family (`NotesBlock`, `FlagNote`), and view/section + isometric + misc-dim annotations (`ViewLabel`, `ViewArrow`, `CuttingPlaneLine`, `IsometricText`, `IsometricLinearDimension`, `ArcLengthDimension`, `JoggedRadiusDimension`). `Explodable.toElements(context?)` takes an optional RenderContext so a view transform bakes into the exported geometry; each class's toSVG derives from the same list. Sheared/rotated text (IsometricText, IsometricLinearDimension value) explodes to upright DXF text (TextElement has no shear/rotation). Every individual annotation is DXF-exportable.
- `sheet.toDXF(options?: { precision?, onUnsupported?(msg) }): string` — whole-sheet R12 DXF (counterpart to `sheet.toSVG()`). Walks content (recursing `Layer`s and `View`s), emits the border on a "BORDER" layer, bakes a `View`'s scale/rotation/translation into geometry (via `Path.transformed`/`applyViewTransform`), and explodes the title block. Native dimensions export as DXF DIMENSION at the sheet/layer level; a native dimension inside a scaled/rotated view can't carry the transform and is reported via `onUnsupported` (not emitted wrong). Entities are typed-layered (VISIBLE/DIMENSIONS/ANNOTATIONS/GDT/TITLEBLOCK/BORDER); SVG `Layer` names aren't mapped to DXF layers. `Layer.getElements()`/`View.getElements()`/`View.viewTransform` expose the tree; `plainBorderElements`/`zonedBorderElements` back the border.
- exportDXF also accepts `BlockInstance` → shared DXF `BLOCK` definition + `INSERT`: each distinct source `Block` written once into BLOCKS (its DrawingElement/TextElement children at local origin, on layer "0"), each placement an INSERT with position/uniform-scale/rotation. Duplicate block names disambiguated (`SYM`,`SYM_2`); unnamed → `BLOCK1`,`BLOCK2`. Only geometry/text inside a block emitted (nested blocks/dimensions skipped). `BlockInstance.placement(): BlockPlacement {block,position,scale,rotationDeg}` exposes what the exporter reads.

### PDF (whole sheet — border, title block, dimensions, GD&T, hatching, everything)
- `exportPDF(sheet: Sheet, options?: { widthMM?, heightMM?, font?: { data: Uint8Array } }): string` — parses `sheet.toSVG()`'s own markup into PDF content ops; `Layer`s become real toggleable PDF Optional Content Groups. Text uses standard Helvetica by default (WinAnsi/Latin-1 only; `⌀`/`⌴`/`⌵` auto-substituted to `Ø`/`CBORE`/`CSK`). Pass `font.data` a `.ttf` or `.otf` to embed it (Type0/Identity-H, ToUnicode) and render arbitrary Unicode — no bundled font, still plain-ASCII/deterministic. glyf TrueType → `FontFile2`, subsetted to used glyphs (composite-aware, ids kept stable, via `subsetFont(data, keepGids)` exported from ttf.ts). OpenType/CFF (OTTO) → the `CFF ` table as `FontFile3` (`/Type1C`, or `/CIDFontType0C` if CID-keyed) in a `CIDFontType0`, glyph-subsetted (CharStrings blanked, ids/subrs/charset kept) via `subsetCFF(cff, keepGids)` exported from ttf.ts — both plain and CID-keyed (FDArray/FDSelect) CFFs. `bold` runs are faux-bolded by stroking the outline. `parseFont` returns `outlineType: "glyf"|"cff"`, `cff?`, `cffIsCID`.

---

## More examples

### GD&T: datum + position tolerance

```ts
import { DatumFeatureSymbol, FeatureControlFrame, circle, centerMark, DrawingElement } from "@invisra/draft";

const edgeMidpoint = { x: 100, y: 150 };
sheet.add(new DatumFeatureSymbol(edgeMidpoint, "A", { angleDeg: 90 }));

const hole = { x: 120, y: 130 };
const r = 4;
sheet.add(new DrawingElement(circle(hole.x, hole.y, r)));
for (const mark of centerMark(hole, r, 2.5)) sheet.add(new DrawingElement(mark, { lineStyle: "centerline" }));

sheet.add(new FeatureControlFrame({ x: 140, y: 100 }, "position", 0.1, {
  diameter: true,
  modifier: "MMC",
  datums: [{ letter: "A" }],
}));
```

### Hatching with a material pattern (holes stay unhatched)

```ts
import { hatchPattern, ANSI32, rectangle, circle, DrawingElement } from "@invisra/draft";

const outer = rectangle(20, 20, 60, 40);
const hole = circle(40, 40, 8);
for (const line of hatchPattern([outer, hole], ANSI32)) sheet.add(line); // ANSI32 = steel
sheet.add(new DrawingElement(outer));
sheet.add(new DrawingElement(hole));
```

### Tolerances: symmetric, asymmetric, and stacked limits

```ts
import { LinearDimension } from "@invisra/draft";

sheet.add(new LinearDimension({ x: 0, y: 0 }, { x: 80, y: 0 }, { offset: -12, orientation: "horizontal", tolerance: 0.1 }));            // "80.00 ±0.10"
sheet.add(new LinearDimension({ x: 0, y: 0 }, { x: 80, y: 20 }, { offset: 10, tolerance: { plus: 0.2, minus: 0.05 } }));                 // "... +0.20/-0.05"
sheet.add(new LinearDimension({ x: 0, y: 20 }, { x: 0, y: 60 }, { offset: 12, orientation: "vertical", tolerance: 0.1, toleranceDisplay: "limits" })); // stacked upper/lower
```

### Multi-sheet set + DXF/PDF export

```ts
import { DrawingSet, Sheet, TitleBlock, DrawingElement, rectangle, exportDXF, exportPDF } from "@invisra/draft";

const set = new DrawingSet();
const geometryElements: DrawingElement[] = [];

set.add(({ sheetLabel }) => {
  const sheet = new Sheet();
  sheet.setTitleBlock(new TitleBlock({ title: "PLATE", drawingNumber: "DRW-2", sheet: sheetLabel }));
  const el = new DrawingElement(rectangle(20, 20, 80, 50));
  geometryElements.push(el);
  sheet.add(el);
  return sheet;
});
set.add(({ sheetLabel }) => {
  const sheet = new Sheet();
  sheet.setTitleBlock(new TitleBlock({ title: "PLATE - DETAIL", drawingNumber: "DRW-2", sheet: sheetLabel }));
  return sheet;
});

const sheets = set.build();          // [sheet1, sheet2], each knows "1 OF 2" / "2 OF 2"
const svgs = sheets.map((s) => s.toSVG());
const dxf = exportDXF(geometryElements);   // geometry only
const pdf = exportPDF(sheets[0]!);         // whole sheet 1, border/title block included
```

## Known gaps (don't assume these exist)

PDF embeds
both glyf `.ttf` and OpenType/CFF `.otf` (plain + CID-keyed), all glyph-subsetted; default (no
options.font) is non-embedded Helvetica (WinAnsi/Latin-1). Full list with citations: README.md "Known gaps".
